content.text:
I created both the dashboard and the alert rule. The rule has already run once and succeeded. I couldn't check whether the dashboard panels draw correctly, because there's no way to view them through the API. The panels saved without errors, but the four built on ES|QL queries are the ones most worth a quick look in the browser.

**1. Data exploration.** The data view `Kibana Sample Data Logs` (index `kibana_sample_data_logs`, time field `timestamp`) holds one document per web request. The useful fields are:
- `response` (the HTTP status code, stored as text)
- `bytes` (response size)
- `clientip`
- `url`, `request` and `extension`
- `geo.src` / `geo.dest` (source and destination country)
- `machine.os`, `agent`, `referer` and `host`

Running queries straight against the data is turned off in this Kibana, so I couldn't look at actual values. The panels are based on the field list plus the known contents of the sample data.

**2. Dashboard "EFF-387cc214 Web logs overview"** (id `97ac9941-6986-4428-9890-097afd0fba9e`, default time range last 7 days) has 7 panels:
- Single-number panels for:
  - Total requests
  - Unique visitors (distinct `clientip`)
  - Average response size in bytes
  - Error rate (percentage of 4xx and 5xx responses)
- A stacked bar chart of requests over time, split by response code
- Top 10 requested URLs
- Top 10 source countries

**3. Alert rule "EFF-387cc214 5xx spike"** (id `fec0beaf-441b-4ded-a375-cf077e2bd901`) is an Elasticsearch query rule:
- It checks every minute.
- It counts requests in the last 5 minutes whose response code is from 500 to 599, using the `timestamp` field.
- It fires when that count is more than 10.

Two things to know about the rule:
- It has no notification set up, so when it fires the alert only shows up in Kibana. Add a notification if you want an email or message.
- I turned off the setting that skips requests already counted in the previous check. Because the 5-minute windows overlap, leaving it on would make the rule miss real spikes.
